title: Understanding Write Amplification in LSM-Trees versus B-Trees
explanation: Database storage engines choose different tradeoffs for read and write performance. Traditional B-Trees update data in place on fixed-size pages. This approach creates high write amplification because minor updates rewrite entire disk pages. Random writes suffer significantly under this model. In contrast, Log-Structured Merge-trees write incoming updates sequentially to an in-memory buffer called a MemTable. Once full, the buffer flushes sequentially to disk as an immutable SSTable. Background compaction processes later merge and clean these sorted tables. This architecture converts random writes into fast sequential writes. However, LSM-trees increase read latency because queries must scan multiple SSTables. Developers must evaluate workload patterns carefully. High-throughput write applications benefit from LSM-trees, whereas read-heavy systems favor B-Trees.
takeaway: Choose LSM-tree engines for write-heavy workloads with sequential access, and use B-Trees when point-read latency is your primary bottleneck.
author: Muhammad Junaeid
